title: 9-slice canvas rendering: implement scale9Grid drawImage slicing in renderSymbolInstance
description:
## Problem

The canvas-based authoring-stage renderer (`packages/core/src/engine/renderer.ts`)
has a known TODO for 9-slice (scale9Grid) rendering:

  // TODO: implement full 9-slice drawImage-based rendering when scale9Grid is set.

When a symbol has `scale9Grid != null` and is placed at a non-1:1 scale, the renderer
falls back to a uniform `ctx.scale()`. This distorts the corners and edges of the symbol
(e.g. a rounded-rectangle button that should keep its corners fixed while its body scales
will appear with stretched corners).

The SWF compiler already emits `DefineScalingGrid` (tag 78) correctly (`compile.ts`
line 502), and Flash 8's runtime respects it. The authoring-stage renderer is the only
missing piece.

## What needs doing

### Implement `renderSymbolInstanceWith9Slice()`
1. Render the symbol to an offscreen canvas at its natural (1:1 scale) size.
2. Split into 9 sectors using the `scale9Grid` rectangle:
   - 4 corners: rendered at 1:1 scale (no stretch)
   - 4 edges: stretched only along one axis
   - 1 center: stretched in both axes
3. Composite all 9 sectors onto the main canvas at the target instance dimensions
   using `ctx.drawImage(offscreen, srcX, srcY, srcW, srcH, dstX, dstY, dstW, dstH)`.
4. Replace the `void has9Slice;` no-op at line 720 with a branch to this new path.

### Unit test
The existing tests in `packages/core/src/engine/__tests__/nineslice.test.ts` and
`scale9grid.test.ts` should be updated/extended to verify pixel output:
- A 2× scaled instance of a symbol with scale9Grid should produce corner pixels that
  match a 1× rendering of just the corner, and edge pixels that are stretched.

## Files involved
- `packages/core/src/engine/renderer.ts` — main change, around `renderSymbolInstance()` line 698
- `packages/core/src/engine/__tests__/nineslice.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/engine/__tests__/scale9grid.test.ts`

## Acceptance criteria
1. A button symbol with `scale9Grid` set and `scaleX: 2, scaleY: 1` renders corners at
   1× scale while the center stretches to fill.
2. No regression on symbols without scale9Grid (most common case).
3. Nineslice unit tests pass including a pixel-level check.
